title: First Toungoo Empire
capsule: The First Toungoo Empire was founded at Toungoo in the Sittaung River valley by Minkyinyo (r. c. 1486–1531), who consolidated Burman power after the fall of Pagan; it is attested here from 1502 to 1756, spanning both the classical Toungoo and the Restored Toungoo periods. Under Tabinshwehti (r. 1531–1550) and his successor Bayinnaung (r. 1551–1581) the empire became the most powerful mainland Southeast Asian state of the sixteenth century, annexing Hanthawaddy (1539), Ava (1555), the Shan States, Lan Na (1558), and briefly Ayutthaya (1569). Bayinnaung's overextended conquests unraveled after his death, and the Restored Toungoo dynasty, ruling from Ava after 1613, maintained a smaller but stable domain until the Konbaung dynasty displaced it in 1752.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Toungoo territorial extent is documented in Burmese royal chronicles (Hmannan Yazawin) and some Portuguese and Dutch sources; core lowland territories are fairly well attested, but highland tributary frontiers with the Shan principalities and Laos are approximate.
